items.prompt: A developer adds noexcept to Ledger::strong but leaves its throw in place, then calls strong(true). What follows if that exception tries to leave the function?

options.text: The caller catch runs after stack unwinding is guaranteed to finish.
options.why: Violation of noexcept calls terminate; normal propagation to the caller handler is not available, and unwinding before termination is not guaranteed.

options.text: The compiler must reject every potentially throwing statement in the body.
options.why: A noexcept function may compile with potentially throwing operations; warnings are not the same as a mandatory language rejection.

options.text: std::terminate is called; noexcept does not supply rollback or recovery.
options.why: The exception may not escape the noexcept boundary normally. Termination is the contract response, not conversion into a result.

options.text: The function returns an error_code while preserving its signature.
options.why: noexcept does not add an error result, translate an exception, or alter the return type.

items.explanation: The exception may not escape the noexcept boundary normally. Termination is the contract response, not conversion into a result.
